Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG OPINION NO. 9 S. 2010 20 January 2010 DIR. LORETO T. BHAGWAM, MNSA, CESO Regional Director DILG-Region X (Northern Mindanao) Masterson Avenue, Km 3 Upper Carmen, Cagayan de Oro City Dear Dir. Bhagwani: This has reterence to your earlier letter requesting our legal opinion and guidance relative to the seemingly conflicting provisions of Section 62 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) pertaining to the prohibition on the imposition of preventive suspension within ninety (90) days immediately prior to any election, and Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Eiection Code (BP 881) pertaining to the ptohibition on suspension of local elective officials during the election period. Your letter was prompted by the promulgation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Lanao del Norte on 05 January 2010 of its Resolution No. 01, series of 2010 recommending the imposition of preventive suspension upon Vice-Mayor Lacson Lantud of Pantao Ragat, Lanao del Norte. In your letter, you initially cited the provision of Section 62 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 relative to the prohibitions on the conduct of administrative investigation and on the imposition of preventive suspension within ninety (90) days immediately prior to any election or beginning 09 February 2010. The foregoing provision, according to you, is apparently in conflict with Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code which prohibits the suspension of local elective officials during election period without prior authority from the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), except when such suspension emanates from the violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, in which case, no prior authority is required. It is your considered view that while there is no legai irnpediment as to date with regard to the provision of Section 62 (c) of the Local Government Code, the provision of the Omnibus Election Code on suspension must prevail. Thus, according to you, suspension cannot anymore be imposed upon the local elective official without prior authority from COMELEC. With all due respect to your view, we are of the considered opinion that Section 62 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991 and Section 261 (x) of the In fact, we find these two (2) Omnibus Election Code are not in conflict. provisions to be complementary to each other.

-2- Pursuant to COMELEC Resolution No. 8646 promulgated on 14 July 2009, the election period has been fixed from 10 January 2010 up to 09 June 2010. During such period and per Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code, no local elective official shall be suspended without prior authority from the COMELEC, except when such suspension is for the purpose of applying the Anti- Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, in which case, no prior authority from the COMELEC is required. We agree with your observation that Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code did not distinguish the nature of the prohibited suspension so that it may include both preventive suspension and suspension as a penalty apptying therefore the settled rufe that where the taw does not distinguish, we should not also distinguish. On the other hand, under Section 62 (c) of the Local Government Code of 1991, no preventive suspension shall be imposed by the Office of the President, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the Sangguniang Panlungsod and the Sangguniang Bayan, in the exercise of their jurisdiction to take cognizance of administrative complaints against elective local officials within their respective disciplinary authonties, within 90 days prior to any election and it one has earlier been imposed, the same shall be automatically lifted at the start of the 90-day period. Along this line, we confirm your computation that the 90-day period prior to the scheduled 10 May 2010 national and local elections shall commence on 09 February 2010. At this juncture, may we note that between the two (2) periods mentioned, that is, the election period under the Omnibus Election Code and the 90-period under the Local Government Code of 1991, the former shall be the first one to set in and in fact has already set in on 10 January 2010. Hence, beginning this period (IO January 2010), no preventive suspension or suspension as a penalty may be imposed by the Office of the President, Sangguniang Panla]awigan, Sangguniang Panlungsod, Sangguniang Bayan or the Ombudsman against elective local officials without the prior authority from COMELEC. In your case, since the imptementation of Resotution No. 01, series of 2010 of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan recommending the imposition of preventive suspension upon Vice-Mayor Lacson Lantud of Pantao Ragat, Lanao del Norte will be effected by Governor Mohammad Khalid Q. Dimaporo when the election period has already set in, Govemor Dimaporo should first seek the prior approval ot COMELEC before its implementation in accordance with Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code. In the event that the COMELEC will approve the implementation of the preventive suspension imposed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan against Vice- Mayor Lacson Lantud, the same can then be implemented but will be automatically lifted on 09 February 2010 in accordance With Section 62 (c) of the Local Govemment Code. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Ls: arb/17/md V truly yours, AUS RE A. PANADERO Undersecretarv
